description.narrative:
Due to the strategic relevance of the contribution and the results achieved by the project, an amendment to the agreement was issued on March 28, 2025, updating the projects objectives and extending the projects implementation period until December 31, 2026, and the validity of the agreement until June 30, 2027.
General Objective Strengthen the institutional, technical, and operational capacity of the Competition Superintendency in Guatemala, ensuring its independence, legitimacy, and effectiveness in promoting a fair and competitive economic environment.
Specific Objectives a) Develop recommendations for the institutional structure required for the effective functioning of the Competition Superintendency, including comparative models of organizational structure, internal regulations, and operational processes.
b) Train key stakeholders in competition law and economic regulation, promoting a culture of competition among professionals, businesses, and civil society.
c) Promote citizen participation and transparency in the selection of the authorities of the Competition Superintendency, ensuring transparency in the process to appoint authorities with independence and legitimacy.
d) Conduct research and diagnostics on competition in strategic sectors of the Guatemalan economy, providing technical inputs for decision-making.
e) Foster international cooperation and the exchange of best practices with other competition authorities at the regional and international levels.

Establish solid and strategic links to involve key political, civil society and economic actors, to promote an informed understanding of the importance of free competition in the economic development and the country prosperity. And support an effective adoption of a competition law

Etablera solida och strategiska länkar för att involvera viktiga politiska, civila samhället och ekonomiska aktörer, för att främja en välgrundad förståelse för vikten av fri konkurrens för den ekonomiska utvecklingen och landets välstånd. Och stödja ett effektivt antagande av en konkurrenslag

description.narrative:
In April 2024, the Embassy of Sweden in Guatemala signed an agreement with the National Business Council CNE, with the primary objective of promoting the application and understanding of the Competition Law in Guatemala, strengthening the technical capacity of the involved parties, and fostering a culture of competition that encourages economic efficiency to position the country as a destination for foreign direct investment. The work of the CNE focused on creating a space for coordination to support the approval of competition regulations. In this regard, various actions were taken to promote the approval of the law, which was passed on November 19, 2024. Decree 322024.
After this approval, the efforts of the Consejo Nacional Empresarial during 2025 were directed toward the implementation of the law and the establishment of the Superintendence of Competition (SICOM), capacity building and promoting regional and international cooperation to seek institutional partnerships with competition authorities from other countries for institutional strengthening.
In that regard, the main results achieved during 2025 are the following:
Technical Assistance and Development of Inputs
a) Oversight, collaboration, and support in the process of selecting the Board of Directors of the Superintendence of Competition. The support was provided to the nominating bodies: Monetary Board, Executive Branch, and Congress of the Republic.
b) Technical Inputs for the Regulation of the Competition Law. A technical document was delivered outlining the proposed structure for the Regulation of the Competition Law. Subsequently, at SICOMs explicit request, comments were submitted on the regulation published by the Superintendence of Competition.
c) Competition Observatory Design Phase and Baseline The Competition Observatory was designed with two components: 1) Identification of legal barriers to competition, to support SICOM in complying with Article 25, paragraph 7 of Decree 322024 (annual report on necessary reforms to promote competition) and Article 120 (report on the repeal of legal provisions that affect competition). 2) Market studies in strategic sectors. The technical committee identified priority sectors such as energy, finance, agroindustry, pharmaceuticals, and taxation, as well as sectors with territorial development potential (tourism, logistics, and infrastructure). In October 2025, research calls were published with Terms of Reference to review regulatory barriers and unnecessary requirements that increase costs and distort competition. The study on the food and beverage sector is already underway, with the final report expected in the first half of January 2026.
d) Competition Manual for Businesses. In December 2025, the Competition Manual for Businesses was completed. Its purpose is to facilitate the private sectors adaptation to the new regulatory environment by providing practical tools to prevent sanction risks, align business conduct with the Competition Law, and strengthen a culture of compliance.
e) Proposal for Amendments to the Law In March 2025, following a detailed analysis of the approved Competition Law, areas for improvement were identified and a proposal for amendments was submitted
Specialized Training and Capacity Building
a) Diploma in Competition Law: From May to December, the first edition of the Diploma in Competition Law was carried out, with 32 participants. The academic program, designed to build technical capacities in competition matters, addressed the economic and legal foundations of competition, practical cases, and international standards. This diploma aims to build an essential knowledge base for the effective implementation of Decree 322024. The 2025 cohort included professionals from the fields of economics, law, public administration, telecommunications, and auditing.
b) Launch of the 2nd Cohort of the Diploma in Competition Law: In December 2025, the call for applications for the second edition of the Diploma in Competition Law was published. The diploma will be delivered from March to September 2026, beginning with an Integration Workshop in February 2026.
c) Training Sessions on Competition Law with the Directorate of Legislative Studies and Research of the Congress of the Republic (DEIL): On November 24, the development of a training program began, designed to strengthen the capacities of Congress in its strategic role in implementing the new Competition Law. The sessions addressed the historical evolution of competition law, the importance of advocacy, the incorporation of the competition principle into regulation, and the use of sectoral studies and public procurement. The program was directed at 49 DEIL staff members and legislative advisors and consisted of six technical sessions delivered by regional specialists. The objective was to raise awareness of how efficient regulatory frameworks, market diagnostics, and public policies aligned with competition contribute to improving economic efficiency, transparency, and investment attraction.
Competition Promotion Activities a) Regional Visits in Guatemala: Across the departments of Chiquimula, Sacatepéquez, Huehuetenango, and Quetzaltenango, regional outreach activities were conducted to present the fundamentals, benefits, and opportunities arising from the newly approved Competition Law. These sessions combined keynote presentations with practical components aimed at identifying local challenges and opportunities for businesses and entrepreneurs. Participation varied across territories, including representatives from entrepreneurship associations, municipalities, executive branch entities, university students, local business owners, and entrepreneurs. Notably, the visits coordinated with Universidad Da Vinci in Huehuetenango and Quetzaltenango gathered 210 and 71 participants respectively, while sessions in Chiquimula and Sacatepéquez engaged 24 and 6 attendees, including the Deputy Director of the Superintendence of Competition. Across all locations, the discussions emphasized the benefits of the law, the institutional formation process, and the emerging opportunities for the private sector.
b) 2025 Annual Competition Congress On February 19, the congress From Approval to Action: Establishing the Superintendence of Competition was held to discuss perspectives on the implementation of the new authority. Eighty participants attended, including former officials from the competition authorities of Costa Rica, El Salvador, Honduras, and the Dominican Republic, as well as nominating entities and candidates.
c) Webinars Five webinars were conducted with the objective of strengthening technical knowledge and promoting the competition law. The webinars delivered are listed below: a) Competition in Strategic Sectors, b) The Importance of Competition in the Public Sector. c) How Was the Competition Law Finalized? d) Competition in the Financial Sector: Regional Lessons and Opportunities for Guatemala. e) The Strategic Agenda of the Superintendence of Competition.
Regional and International Cooperation a) Signing of the Letter of Understanding with the Superintendency of Competition of El Salvador b) CompiteGuate joins the Academic Society for Competition Law (ASCOLA) c) Introductory Meeting with FUSADES (El Salvador) (Salvadoran Foundation for Economic and Social Development) d) Introductory Meeting with the Competition Center of the Adolfo Ibáñez University (Chile)
Advocacy and Strategic Communication a) With the purpose of positioning, promoting, and disseminating the CompiteGuate initiative and its mission to establish a solid culture of competition, a comprehensive multisectoral communication strategy was implemented. As communication is an essential crosscutting component of the initiative, efforts were coordinated across key areas, ranging from technical training and the creation of strategic alliances to the oversight required for the establishment of the competition authority. As part of the content and dissemination strategy, infographics and informational videos were produced and published across social media platforms, including Instagram, Facebook, and X. The content addressed key topics such as: a) Myths and realities of the Competition Law. b) Benefits and strengthening effects of a Competition Law. c) Impact indicators of the Competition Law. d) Powers and responsibilities of a competition authority. d) CompiteGuate glossary
